FINAL ORDER ON REQUEST FOR ATTORNEY’S FEES
The Administra(cid:415)ve Law Judge (“ALJ”) Vanessa Voigt Gould, having reviewed the record in
this proceeding including, but not limited to, Respondent Northern Indiana Manufacturing, Inc.’s
(“NIM”) Request for A(cid:425)orney’s Fees, the Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)oner the Indiana Department of Environmental
Management’s (“IDEM”) Response, NIM’s Reply to the IDEM’s Response, and the IDEM’s Sur-
Reply, now issues this Final Order denying NIM’s request for a(cid:425)orney’s fees. Any aggrieved party
may appeal this decision. Appeal instruc(cid:415)ons are at the end of this document.
Jurisdic(cid:415)on
The ALJ assigned to this proceeding by the Director of the Office of Administra(cid:415)ve Law
Proceedings (“OALP”), see Ind. Code § 4-15-10.5-13, has jurisdic(cid:415)on over this case pursuant to
Indiana Code § 4-15-10.5-12, which gives OALP jurisdic(cid:415)on over agency administra(cid:415)ve ac(cid:415)ons
subject to the Indiana Administra(cid:415)ve Orders and Procedures Act at Indiana Code Art. 4-21.5
(AOPA) or “any other statute that requires or allows the office to take ac(cid:415)on.” The OALP has
jurisdic(cid:415)on over this case because this case is governed by AOPA.
Issue
Whether NIM is en(cid:415)tled to a(cid:425)orney’s fees under Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5.

Procedural History
1. NIM filed a Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)on for Administra(cid:415)ve Review (“Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)on”) with the Office of
Environmental Adjudica(cid:415)on (“OEA”) on December 31, 2019.
2. That same day the proceeding was assigned to Chief Environmental Law Judge (“ELJ”)
Mary Davidson.
3. The Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)on presented seven issues for review:
a. Whether NIM is exempt from liability arising under Ind. Code § 13-25-4-1, et seq.
b. Whether Dynamic Alliance (“Dynamic”) should be held solely and 100%
responsible for the inves(cid:415)ga(cid:415)on and remedia(cid:415)on of the site.
c. Whether IDEM failed to pursue all avenues of recovery against the actual polluter.
d. Whether the claims against NIM were arbitrary, capricious, and/or an abuse of
discre(cid:415)on.
e. Whether the Order was void for vagueness under Indiana law.
f. Whether the vagueness of the Order violated due process and due course of law
rights under the U.S. Cons(cid:415)tu(cid:415)on and Indiana Cons(cid:415)tu(cid:415)on.
g. Whether the Order or IDEM's implementa(cid:415)on of the Order violates NIM's due
process and due course of law rights under the U.S. Cons(cid:415)tu(cid:415)on, the Indiana
Cons(cid:415)tu(cid:415)on, the Indiana AOPA, or other Indiana law.
4. On May 11, 2022, this proceeding was reassigned to ELJ Lori Kyle Endris.
5. On June 19, 2023, the IDEM filed a Mo(cid:415)on for Judgment on the Pleadings and a brief in
support thereof, which was later converted to a Mo(cid:415)on for Summary Judgment through
the filing of an affidavit in support.
6. On June 20, 2023, NIM filed a Mo(cid:415)on for Summary Judgment along with a brief in support
thereof.
7. Briefing on summary judgment was completed by the par(cid:415)es in August of 2023.
8. Oral Argument on summary judgment was held on September 11, 2023. Therea(cid:332)er, both
par(cid:415)es submi(cid:425)ed proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law.
9. On January 31, 2024, ALJ Endris issued a Final Order Denying in favor of the IDEM holding
that:
a. NIM was not exempt from liability arising under Ind. Code under Ind. Code § 13-
25-4-1.
b. OEA did not have the authority to hold Dynamic solely responsible for the
inves(cid:415)ga(cid:415)on and remedia(cid:415)on of the Site.
c. IDEM had not failed to pursue all avenues of recovery against the actual polluter.
d. The Commissioner’s Order was not un(cid:415)mely in that neither CERCLA’s six-year cost
recovery statute, Indiana's 10-year residual statute of limita(cid:415)ons, nor the doctrine
of laches applied.

e. All other issues presented in the Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)on had been abandoned by NIM on
Summary Judgment and had therefore been waived.
10. On March 1, 2024, NIM sought judicial review of the Final Order in the Marion County
Superior Court, Civil Division 13, before the Hon. James A. Joven.
11. On December 30, 2024, Judge Joven issued an Order Gran(cid:415)ng Relief on Judicial Review
reversing the Final Order finding: "IDEM brought its enforcement ac(cid:415)on beyond the ten-
year limita(cid:415)on period for any cause of ac(cid:415)on not limited by any other statute, as set forth
by Ind. Code § 34-11-1-2. IDEM's ac(cid:415)on is, therefore, un(cid:415)mely. Accordingly, pursuant to
Indiana Code §§4-21.5-5-14(d) and -15, the Court SETS ASIDE the OEA's Order and
REMANDS the case to address Northern's en(cid:415)tlement to a(cid:425)orney's fees under Indiana
Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5."
12. On May 8, 2025, NIM filed a Request for Award of A(cid:425)orney’s Fees with the OALP. 1
13. On May 19, 2025, this proceeding was reassigned to ALJ Vanessa Voigt Gould.
14. On May 23, 2025, the IDEM filed its Response to NIM’s Request for A(cid:425)orney’s Fees.
15. On May 30, 2025, NIM filed a Reply to IDEM’s Response on A(cid:425)orney’s Fees.
16. On June 3, 2025, IDEM sought leave to file a Sur-Reply.
17. On June 9, 2025, IDEM’s request for leave to file a Sur-Reply was granted and the IDEM’s
Sur-Reply was incorporated into the record.
Findings of Fact
1. The Commissioner of the IDEM issued an Order to Compel Response Ac(cid:415)on
(“Commissioner’s Order”) related to a 1978 spill of perchloroethylene (“PCE”), and the
resul(cid:415)ng contamina(cid:415)on of an industrial manufacturing site located at 914 Broadway
Street, Chesterton, Porter County, Indiana (“Site”) on December 13, 2019.2
2. The Commissioner’s Order was issued pursuant Ind. Code § 13-25-4-9 and sought to
“compel the implementa(cid:415)on of appropriate response ac(cid:415)vi(cid:415)es in regard to past and
ongoing releases of hazardous substances at the Site.”
3. The Commissioner’s Order was issued to the former owner of the Site - Dynamic Alliance,
Inc. - and the current owner - NIM.
4. NIM (cid:415)mely sought administra(cid:415)ve review of the Commissioner’s Order by filing its Pe(cid:415)(cid:415)on
on December 31, 2019.
1 On July 1, 2024, following the enactment of House Bill 1003, the OEA was eliminated and all proceedings under its
jurisdic(cid:415)on were transferred to the Office of Administra(cid:415)ve Law Proceedings.
2 VCF No. 82879333.

Conclusions of Law
1. This proceeding is properly before the OALP on remand pursuant to Indiana Code § 4-21.5.
2. OALP has jurisdic(cid:415)on over both the subject proceeding and the par(cid:415)es to this ac(cid:415)on and is
the ul(cid:415)mate authority. Ind. Code § 4-21.5-4; Ind. Code §§ 4-15-10.5-12 and 13.
3. The party challenging the agency’s ac(cid:415)on has the burden of proof by a preponderance of the
evidence. IC 4-21.5-3-27.5(a)(1).
4. “With respect to a(cid:425)orney fees, Indiana generally adheres to the American rule whereby each
party bears its own a(cid:425)orney fees absent an agreement between the par(cid:415)es, a statute, or
other rule to the contrary.” Song v. Iatarola, 76 N.E.3d 926, 938 (Ind. Ct. App. 2017), reh'g
granted on other grounds, 83 N.E.3d 80 (Ind. Ct. App. 2017), trans. denied.
5. At the (cid:415)me this proceeding was commenced, there was no statute or rule that would
authorize an ALJ to award a party reasonable a(cid:425)orney’s fees in an adjudica(cid:415)ve proceeding
under AOPA in devia(cid:415)on of the American rule. See, e.g., Heller Development, 2008 OEA 57
("OEA has not been authorized by the legislature to impose legal fees .... ").
6. However, in 2021 the Indiana legislature added a new sec(cid:415)on to AOPA - Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-
27.5 - which authorized an administra(cid:415)ve law judge to order an agency to pay reasonable
a(cid:425)orney fees to a party challenging an agency ac(cid:415)on if it could demonstrate that the ac(cid:415)on
was frivolous, groundless, or pursued in bad faith. Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5.
7. In its originally enacted form, Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5 read:
In a proceeding under this chapter concerning an agency ac(cid:415)on, the administra(cid:415)ve
law judge shall order the agency to pay the reasonable a(cid:425)orney's fees incurred in
the proceeding by the party challenging the agency ac(cid:415)on if the party challenging
the agency ac(cid:415)on proves, by a preponderance of the evidence, that: (1) the
agency's ac(cid:415)on was frivolous or groundless; or (2) the agency pursued the ac(cid:415)on
in bad faith.
This new sec(cid:415)on of AOPA became effec(cid:415)ve on the date of its enactment - July 1, 2021.
8. The Indiana legislature amended Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5 in 2023. The 2023 amendments
added a requirement to the exis(cid:415)ng statutory framework that the party seeking reasonable
a(cid:425)orney’s fee must be the “prevailing party”. See Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5 (2023). The 2023
amendments also added two new grounds for an award of reasonable a(cid:425)orney’s fees if said
prevailing party could prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the agency ac(cid:415)on at
issue was based on an invalid rule or the agency failed to demonstrate that it acted within its

legal authority. See Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5 (2) and (3) (2023). The 2023 amendments took
effect on July 1, 2023.
9. In conjunc(cid:415)on with the 2023 amendments to Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5, the Indiana
legislature enacted Ind. Code § 4-21.5-2-8 which states that the “amendments made to IC 4-
21.5-3-27.5… in the 2023 session of the general assembly only apply to agency ac(cid:415)ons
commenced under IC 4-21.5-3 a(cid:332)er June 30, 2023.”
10. In 2024, the Indiana legislature amended Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5 for a second (cid:415)me. The
2024 amendments slightly modified the structure of Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5 and changed
the “based on an invalid rule” language added in 2023 to “unsupported by a statute or valid
rule”. See Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5(a)(2) (2024). The 2024 amendment also included the
addi(cid:415)on of subsec(cid:415)on (b) which allows for a trial court to award reasonable a(cid:425)orney’s fees in
a judicial review proceeding. See Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5(b) (2024). The 2024 amendments
took effect on July 1, 2024.
11. In its Request for an Award of A(cid:425)orney’s Fees, NIM ini(cid:415)ally concedes that the 2023 and 2024
amendments to Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5 do not apply to this proceeding pursuant to Ind.
Code § 4-21.5-2-8. See NIM’s Request for Award of A(cid:425)orney’s Fees, footnote 3. NIM then
argues that it is en(cid:415)tled to an award of a(cid:425)orney’s fees under Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5, as
originally enacted in 2021, because the agency ac(cid:415)on at issue here was frivolous and
groundless. Conversely, in its Reply to IDEM’s Response to NIM’s Request for A(cid:425)orney’s Fees,
NIM changes course and argues that it is asking the OALP to award a(cid:425)orney’s fees under
subparts (a)(1)(A) and (a)(3) of Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5, cites to the 2024 version of the
statute, and proffers that Judge Joven’s Order Gran(cid:415)ng Relief on Judicial Review confirms not
only that IDEM’s ac(cid:415)on was frivolous or groundless but that it is equally evident that the IDEM
has not demonstrated that it acted within its legal authority.
12. “Whether a statute or amendment is to be applied retroac(cid:415)vely to pending cases or only
prospec(cid:415)vely depends upon the legislature's intent. Absent an express indica(cid:415)on otherwise,
we presume that the legislature intends statutes and amendments to apply prospec(cid:415)vely.”
Chesnut v. Roof, 665 N.E.2d 7, 9 (Ind. Ct. App. 1996). See also Guzzo v. Town of St. John, 131
N.E.3d 179, 180 (Ind. 2019). As more fully explained by the Indiana Court Appeals in Indiana
Bureau of Motor Vehicles v. Watson, 70 N.E.3d 380, 385 (Ind. Ct. App. 2017):
The general rule in Indiana is that “[s]tatutes are to be given prospec(cid:415)ve effect
only, unless the legislature unequivocally and unambiguously intended
retrospec(cid:415)ve effect as well.” State v. Pelley, 828 N.E.2d 915, 919 (Ind. 2005). An
excep(cid:415)on to this general rule exists for remedial or procedural statutes. Mar(cid:415)n v.
Office of Administra(cid:415)ve Law Proceedings Administra(cid:415)ve Case No: IDEM-1912-000556
100 N. Senate Ave., N-802, Indianapolis, IN 46204 5 of 8

2025 OALP 065, page 070

State, 774 N.E.2d 43, 44 (Ind. 2002). Although statutes and rules that are
procedural or remedial may be applied retroac(cid:415)vely, they are not required to be.
Pelley, 828 N.E.2d at 919. Even for procedural or remedial statutes, “retroac(cid:415)ve
applica(cid:415)on is the excep(cid:415)on, and such laws are normally to be applied
prospec(cid:415)vely absent strong and compelling reasons.” Hurst v. State, 890 N.E.2d
88, 95 (Ind. Ct. App. 2008) (quota(cid:415)on omi(cid:425)ed), trans. denied.
A remedial statute is a statute enacted to cure a defect, clear up any confusion and/or mischief
in the prior law, or address silence in a statute. See N.G. v. State, 148 N.E.3d 971, 973 (Ind.
2020), Lawrence v. State, 214 N.E.3d 361, 363 (Ind. 2023), Mar(cid:415)n v. State, 774 N.E.2d 43, 44
(Ind. 2002). A procedural statute is a statute that “prescribes the method of enforcing a right
or obtaining redress for invasion of that right” as opposed to a substan(cid:415)ve statute which
“creates, defines and regulates rights.” Morrison v. Vasquez, 124 N.E.3d 1217, 1222 (Ind.
2019) ci(cid:415)ng Hayden v. State, 771 N.E.2d 100, 102 (Ind. Ct. App. 2002).
13. The Indiana legislature did not specify that Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5 should be given
retrospec(cid:415)ve effect when originally enacted in 2021. Nothing in the plain language of the
statute itself – as originally enacted or as it reads today - indicates an unequivocal and
unambiguous retrospec(cid:415)ve intent. In fact, the only unequivocal and unambiguous intent
expressed by the legislature as to Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5 is that it is not to be given
retrospec(cid:415)ve effect. See Ind. Code § 4-21.5-2-8.
14. Further, Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5 is neither procedural nor remedial. It was not enacted to
cure any defect, clear up confusion, or speak to silence in a preexis(cid:415)ng statute – it was a new
provision enacted to create a new right to a(cid:425)orney's fees outside of the American rule where
none existed previously. Nor does it prescribe a method of enforcing a right or obtaining
redress. Rather, Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5 creates, defines, and regulates a party’s right to
a(cid:425)orney’s fees in an adjudica(cid:415)ve proceeding under AOPA and is thereby substan(cid:415)ve. Because
Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5 is a substan(cid:415)ve statute, the exclusion to the general rule does not
apply.
15. NIM has not presented any evidence or argument to show that Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5 – as
originally enacted or as amended - was intended to have retrospec(cid:415)ve effect. Similarly, NIM
has not presented any evidence or argument that Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5 is procedural or
remedial thereby excep(cid:415)ng it from the general rule that statutes are to be given prospec(cid:415)ve
effect only and are not to be applied retroac(cid:415)vely.
Office of Administra(cid:415)ve Law Proceedings Administra(cid:415)ve Case No: IDEM-1912-000556
100 N. Senate Ave., N-802, Indianapolis, IN 46204 6 of 8

16. Accordingly, Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5 may not be applied retroac(cid:415)vely to create an
en(cid:415)tlement to a(cid:425)orney’s fees in proceedings commenced prior to its enactment and is
thereby inapplicable to this proceeding.
17. NIM has failed to prove, by a preponderance of the evidence, that it is en(cid:415)tled to an award of
a(cid:425)orney’s fees under Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5.
Decision and Order
NIM is not en(cid:415)tled to a(cid:425)orney’s fees under Ind. Code § 4-21.5-3-27.5 and as such, it is
hereby ORDERED that NIM‘s Request for an Award of A(cid:425)orney’s Fees is DENIED.
SO ORDERED on: July 15, 2025.

Appeal Rights
A person who wishes to seek judicial review of this final determina(cid:415)on must file a pe(cid:415)(cid:415)on for
review in an appropriate court within 30 days of the date this Order was served. See Ind. Code §
4-21.5-5-5. Guidance for calcula(cid:415)ng deadlines may be found at Indiana Code § 4-21.5-3-2.
Other requirements for a pe(cid:415)(cid:415)on for judicial review may be found at Indiana Code chapter 4-
21.5-5. A pe(cid:415)(cid:415)on for judicial review must be served on the Office of Administra(cid:415)ve Law at
oalp@oalp.in.gov to ensure the Office prepares the record that will be filed in the court
presiding over the judicial review.
